name: Monounsaturated fat
what_is: Monounsaturated fat is a type of fat whose fatty acids contain one double bond. Oleic acid is one of the most common examples.
why_botia: Monounsaturated fat forms part of total fat, but it is not always declared separately. BOTIA keeps a declared value distinct from total fat and from the regulatory information and evidence used to interpret it.
can_1: Read the monounsaturated fat value when it is declared on the nutrition label and preserve its unit and basis.
can_2: Show that the value forms part of total fat rather than being added to it.
can_3: Connect the declared value with the applicable regulatory information and documented evidence where relevant.
cannot_1: Determine the amount of individual monounsaturated fatty acids from the combined value.
cannot_2: Calculate monounsaturated fat reliably from total fat and other declared fat values.
cannot_3: Treat an undeclared monounsaturated fat value as zero.
